title: Compact exporter stack and span flush smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We are seeing increased tail latency and bursty CPU spikes in the observability pipeline during traffic surges. Root cause analysis points to a combination of: (1) heavyweight exporter initialization and synchronous flushes from multiple services, (2) an old metrics client that allocates large object graphs per metric emission, and (3) tracing hooks that use reflection-heavy pathing for context extraction. This ticket consolidates exporters into a compact, shared export pipeline, replaces the legacy metrics client with a lightweight emitter shim, and implements a span flush smoothing algorithm to stagger flushes and reduce tail spikes. The goal is a measurable reduction in p95/p99 telemetry latency and lower CPU variance under load while keeping semantic compatibility with existing dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: p95 telemetry export latency reduced by >= 30% in the synthetic surge benchmark (same load profile)
p99 telemetry export latency reduced by >= 20%
CPU variance during 2x traffic burst lowered by >= 40% across staging canaries
No metric name or label fidelity regressions in dashboards for top-50 metrics (manual sample + automated diff)
All services default to the shared exporter without requiring code changes (config opt-out supported)
Unit and integration tests for the emitter shim and flush scheduler added with >= 95% coverage for new code paths
tasks: Add compact exporter coordinator library with a bounded worker pool and batched payloads
Implement span flush smoothing: jittered flush windows and backpressure-aware staggering
Prototype a lightweight metrics emitter API and migrate two high-volume services as canaries
Replace reflection-based context extraction in tracing hooks with a fast-path helper and fallback
Create a compatibility layer so legacy exporters can be bridged to the new coordinator
Add smoke and load tests in CI that emulate surge patterns used in the postmortem
Instrument dashboards to show exporter queue depth, flush jitter distribution, and emitter allocation rate
Prepare rollout plan: canary by service group, monitor 72 hours, automatic rollback threshold
notes: Trade-offs considered: moving to a single shared exporter reduces duplication and memory use but adds a central bottleneck risk; mitigated via bounded workers and per-tenant queues.
Decided against wholesale OTLP gRPC compression changes in this ticket to keep scope limited; compression tuning deferred to ENG-18010.
Emitter shim intentionally preserves metric names and labeling semantics to avoid dashboard churn; internal metric IDs are remapped but not exposed.
Performance hotspot: the old metrics client allocated temporary maps per emission. The emitter will reuse pooled buffers and preallocate label slices for common metrics.
Tracing hook change requires a brief compatibility period where both fast-path and reflection fallback are enabled; fast-path gated behind feature flag 'trace.fast_path_v2'.
risks: Centralizing exporters may increase blast radius for misbehaving payloads; mitigated by per-tenant admission control and circuit breakers.
Subtle metric renaming bugs could impact billing dashboards if not caught by the diff tests—added manual verification step for billing team.
Large services might need tuning of worker pool sizes; default conservative config will be used and surfaced in runtime config docs.
